lines: When Sweet Clara was twelve years old, she was taken from her mother and sent to Home Plantation as a field worker.
She could not handle the hard work of the fields.
So her Aunt Rachel taught Clara how to sew so that she could avoid the terrible conditions out in the fields.
Clara became very good at it and was moved into the Big House to sew full time.
The sewing room was just next to the kitchen.
She soon learned about the Underground Railroad, which led some slaves to Canada for freedom.
There was one difficulty with escape — there was no map to help slaves on their way to freedom.
Clara began to draw a map of the escape path on the ground.
She soon realized that the map on the ground would wash away.
However, she could create a map in fabric and it would remain.
She began collecting pieces of fabric as she sewed.
The work took a long time.
Months could pass while she waited for a piece of fabric in the right color: blue for streams and rivers, green for fields, and white for roads.
The more information Clara got, the larger her map became.
Finally, Clara completed the path to freedom.
Aunt Rachel watched her get ready to leave.
Aunt Rachel thought about going with her.
But then she said, “Leave me your map.
I’m too old to go with you.
Maybe I can help others follow the map to freedom.”
Kissing her, Clara answered, “I think it should stay here.
It’s okay because I have a map in my memory.”
And then her map served as a guide to other slaves looking for freedom.
